source.scalePaper: Donnellan, M. B., Oswald, F. L., Baird, B. M., & Lucas, R. E. (2006). The Mini-IPIP scales: Tiny-yet-effective measures of the Big Five factors of personality. Psychological Assessment, 18, 192-203.
source.administrationOrderNote: Items are stored in the commonly reprinted 1–20 order. Keys match the IPIP Mini-IPIP scoring key, not a local paraphrase.
source.directionsNote: Project-original instructions; the English items and key are from IPIP.

directions.text: Rate how well each statement describes your usual behavior today. Use the five options shown below.

signNotes.neuroticism: Mini-IPIP Factor IV is Neuroticism, not Emotional Stability. Positive-keyed items raise Neuroticism. Negative-keyed items (relaxed; seldom feel blue) lower Neuroticism and therefore point toward the emotional-stability end. Emotional stability is the opposite pole, not a second score. IPIP's key page states that the authors scored the lexical Emotional Stability scale in reverse and labeled it Neuroticism. This program does not convert either pole into a number.
signNotes.intellect: Mini-IPIP Factor V is Intellect or Imagination. It is not broad Openness to Experience. The IPIP key page notes that this short scale comes from the lexical Big Five markers, not the IPIP Five-Factor Model inventory. Only one item is positively keyed (vivid imagination); the other three are reverse-keyed. Novelty talk is not scored as this factor.

ipipKeyFootnote: The authors of the Mini-IPIP chose to score the Emotional Stability scale from the lexical Big Five in reverse and to use the label Neuroticism from the Five-Factor Model for this scale. The current consensus is that Emotional Stability and Neuroticism are opposite ends of the same dimension, or nearly so.
keyMeaning: + means agreement raises the named factor. - means agreement lowers it (reverse-keyed on the original 1–5 scale). This program does not score responses.

items.text: Am the life of the party.
Am not interested in other people's problems.
Often forget to put things back in their proper place.
Am relaxed most of the time.
Am not interested in abstract ideas.
Talk to a lot of different people at parties.
Am not really interested in others.
Do not have a good imagination.
